root_cause.text: In pn532_receive_buf(), the receive skb is allocated after consuming bytes and after potentially handing a complete frame, so if allocation fails, the function incorrectly returns 0 despite having consumed bytes, breaking the serdev accounting contract and leaving recv_skb NULL for subsequent use, leading to a NULL dereference.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explains: "The current code consumes bytes into recv_skb and may already hand a complete frame to pn533_recv_frame() before allocating a fresh receive buffer. If that alloc_skb() fails, the callback returns 0 even though it has already consumed bytes, and it leaves recv_skb as NULL for the next receive callback. That breaks the receive_buf() accounting contract and can also lead to a NULL dereference on the next skb_put_u8()." The patch moves the allocation to the beginning of the loop and returns i on failure, and sets recv_skb to NULL after handing a frame instead of attempting to allocate immediately.

candidates.rationale: Allocation of new skb after consuming bytes; failure leads to NULL recv_skb and incorrect return value.
Check for allocation failure; but returning 0 is incorrect.
Returning 0 on allocation failure breaks serdev accounting and leaves recv_skb NULL.
Handing off the previous frame before allocating new skb; if allocation fails, recv_skb is NULL for next call.
Part of the frame handling flow that triggers the trimming and subsequent allocation.
Trims the skb before sending it; part of the receive logic that contributes to the sequence.
Loop that processes each byte; the count variable is used for the incorrect return value.
Part of the loop structure within the receive function.
Deletes timer at start of receive; not directly causing vulnerability but part of the function.

vuln_statements.explanation: Allocation of the receive skb after potentially handing off a complete frame. If this allocation fails, dev->recv_skb becomes NULL, leading to a NULL dereference on the next call.
Check for allocation failure. The subsequent return 0 is incorrect as bytes have already been consumed.
Returns 0 on allocation failure despite having consumed bytes, breaking the serdev accounting contract and leaving recv_skb NULL for subsequent use.
Hands off the completed receive frame before allocating a new skb. If the subsequent allocation fails, recv_skb is NULL and the next call will dereference it.
Part of the frame handling flow that triggers the trimming of the current skb, leading to the eventual allocation of a new one. Contributes to the sequence where allocation failure causes the bug.
Trims the skb before sending the frame. This is part of the receive logic that sets up the condition for the new allocation, which may fail and cause the vulnerability.

Loop that consumes bytes from the serial device. The count of bytes consumed is later supposed to be returned, but if allocation fails inside the loop, the early return 0 incorrectly reports no bytes consumed.

bic_trace_step.reason: In pn532_receive_buf (lines 165-178), after detecting a complete frame and calling pn533_recv_frame, the code allocates a new skb with alloc_skb. If the allocation fails, it returns 0 without preserving the skb pointer (dev->recv_skb becomes NULL) and without accounting for the bytes already consumed (i). This leads to a NULL pointer dereference on subsequent use and breaks the serdev accounting contract, as described in the root cause.
